skill.name: writing-types
skill.description: Guides modular TypeScript type and interface writing for a Next.js app, with files organized under srs/types.
skill.summary: Write small, modular TypeScript types and interfaces for a Next.js app.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Both static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around the srs/types path. SKILL.md contains only prose instructions for organizing TypeScript types and interfaces, with no executable code or command instructions. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or other semantic abuse.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 3 uses backticks only as Markdown inline code formatting for the srs/types path. It is not Ruby or shell execution and does not instruct the model to run commands.
Line 8 repeats the srs/types path in Markdown inline code within a prose instruction. There is no executable code, shell command, or user-controlled command construction.

content.value_statement: Next.js projects can collect large type files that are hard to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to write small TypeScript types and interfaces in srs/types.
actual_capabilities: Guides writing TypeScript types and interfaces for a Next.js app.
Encourages modular type files instead of large shared files.
Directs output toward the srs/types folder used by the skill.
Recommends separating types and interfaces across files when useful.
Limits generated files to 50 lines where practical.
limitations: Does not include project-specific type definitions or examples.
Does not validate TypeScript syntax or run project tests.
Assumes the target folder is srs/types, as written in the skill.
Provides style guidance only, not a complete architecture standard.

use_cases.title: Create feature types
use_cases.description: Define compact types and interfaces for a new Next.js feature without growing a shared type file.

use_cases.title: Split crowded definitions
use_cases.description: Refactor a large type collection into smaller files that are easier to scan and maintain.

use_cases.title: Review type organization
use_cases.description: Check whether proposed type files follow the modular structure and file length guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic types
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-types skill to create TypeScript types and interfaces for a profile settings feature in a Next.js app.

prompt_templates.title: Organize by domain
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for several related models
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-types skill to organize order, customer, and payment type definitions into modular files under srs/types.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor large type files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-types skill to split an oversized type file into smaller files while preserving clear names and imports.

prompt_templates.title: Audit type structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-types skill to review these proposed Next.js type definitions for modularity, file size, and interface placement.

output_examples.input: Create types for a user profile settings page.
output_examples.output: The response proposes separate profile, preferences, and notification type files, each kept short and focused.

output_examples.input: Split a long list of checkout interfaces.
output_examples.output: The response groups checkout, payment, and address definitions into separate files with clear naming.
The response flags crowded files, suggests smaller modules, and checks whether files stay near the 50 line limit.

best_practices: Give the feature name, expected data shapes, and current folder layout.
Ask for small files with clear names before requesting implementation code.
Review generated imports and names against your project conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not place unrelated domain models in one shared type file.
Do not ask the skill to run TypeScript checks or project tests.
Do not treat the 50 line rule as more important than readable definitions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps write modular TypeScript types and interfaces for a Next.js app.

faq.question: Which folder does it target?
faq.answer: The skill targets srs/types, matching the path stated in its instructions.

faq.question: Does it create runtime code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on type and interface organization, not runtime behavior.

faq.question: Can it validate TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. It does not run TypeScript, linters, or tests.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help split large type files and review type organization.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
